subject: Client-observed short rock-slope climb candidate from detached S5 route11 stop
scope: Read-only comparison of two isolated original-client 1.16.5.0 copied-harness traces at the same dry-bank rock slope. Both used reset copied mission timers; neither establishes the original final-live route or timer sufficiency. No new client run or gameplay change.

sources.location: last pre-hold view beside steep rock slope
lines 39-49, prior accepted climb and subsequent wreck-approach movement
accepted positions corresponding to driver-pre.log lines 39-49

observations.finding: The detached run stopped at (-168.08594,91.40625,-16.875) after a 0.23 m target-progress packet. The pre-hold screenshot shows a steep rock face directly ahead/left. This is an approach constraint, not proof that the slope cannot be climbed.

An earlier independent copied-client route from nearby (-167.02344,90.80078,-16.042969) accepted (-168.54297,91.46875,-16.929688), then (-170.20312,93.28125,-19.15625), then (-169.96875,94.40234,-20.730469). The first of these lies only about 0.46 m west of the detached stop. That run continued toward (-171.39844,93.859375,-21.339844) and ultimately reached (-179.71875,91.66797,-24.792969), so the slope has been traversed by the normal client in one copied run.

Path queries from the detached stop to the prior accepted climb positions return complete paths, with intermediate corners near (-170.4,92.3,-17.6) and (-170.4,93.5,-18.8). But the query snaps the start from (-168.08594,91.40625,-16.875) to (-169.21092,92.46565,-17.15625), about 1.16 m horizontally and 1.06 m upward. Thus the navmesh is a loose geometry cross-check, not reliable evidence that a direct heading from the actual client position will clear the rock.

bounded_next_test.confidence: moderate for local reachability, low for an exact repeat from the new stop
bounded_next_test.action: If a future isolated run reaches the detached stop again, try one very short westward adjustment toward the first prior accepted point. Require a fresh accepted Move and inspect the screenshot/height before continuing. Then aim for the prior accepted climb points in short holds, using a bounded window that examines all fresh packets and positive target progress. If the first point cannot be reached or the player slips downslope, stop; do not assert a hard collision from one small packet. Once the third point is client-verified, resume the earlier accepted route toward (-171.39844,93.859375,-21.339844) and then the wreck corridor.

limits: The earlier copied-client route succeeded locally but is not a retail final-live route capture.
The first candidate point is under 0.5 m away, near movement telemetry resolution, and may require judging actual clearance by screenshot rather than a 0.35 m target threshold alone.
No new normal-client test from the detached stop was run; S6 research owns the shared harness currently.
